column2: ROSINA, died 19 January 1952, register NR. 133, is at page 127 as "geb. Langner verw. Moerke" under L and at page 141 as "Moerke geb. Langner" under M. Same woman, same date, same number. AND A USEFUL NUANCE: Nr. 479, "geb. Lemke verw. Meyer, Ernestine, 3.3.52", sits in the L block and has NO twin in M — the M run goes 466, 481 with nothing between. So the maiden-name entry can stand ALONE. That asymmetry runs in the direction that helps: the register never drops the maiden-name entry, only sometimes the married one. READING L IS ENOUGH.

THIS VOLUME TRIPPED THE SIZE ALARM AND SURVIVED IT. 376 pages for two years against Nr. 585's 275 for two is 188 pages a year against 137 — a 37 per cent jump, which is exactly the Kreuzberg-1982 signature. So the whole book was probed, not just the middle: B at 20, G at 100, L at 180, R at 260, S at 300, U at 340, W at 360, Z at 374. ONE MONOTONIC ALPHABET, NO SECOND SEQUENCE. The extra bulk is a new layout, not extra names — see the next row.

column1: *** AND THE NEW LAYOUT MATTERS, BECAUSE IT BREAKS ONE OF THE THREE CHECKS ***
column2: From 1954 the register groups each letter-year BY MONTH, under a red-underlined Januar, Februar, März heading. Those heading lines eat pages, which is where the 37 per cent went. THE CONSEQUENCE: register numbers are no longer monotonic across a whole year, so "the last number of each page must reach the first of the next" IS NO LONGER A VALID CONTINUITY TEST on its own. Replace it with: consecutive page numbers, the half-overlap confirmed by a row appearing in both halves, AND the month headings running Januar to Dezember in order with none missing. All three held for 1954 and 1955.

# ---------------- THE THREE THINGS THAT MUST BE TRUE BEFORE A YEAR COUNTS ----------------
*** 1. BOUNDED AT BOTH ENDS ***
column2: a page that OPENS the letter at a low register number (single or double digits), and a page that CLOSES it into blank ruled lines or a printed footer. If either end is missing the year is NOT done, however many pages were read.

column1: *** 2. CONTINUOUS ACROSS EVERY PAGE BOUNDARY ***
column2: the last register number of each page must reach the first of the next. A GAP MEANS A MISSED PAGE. This is the check that catches a cropped screenshot, and it is the only one that does.

column1: *** 3. EVERY PAGE READ IN TWO HALVES ***
column2: never one screenshot per page. See the method below.

column1: *** 4. AND THE REASON READING ONLY THE L BLOCK IS ENOUGH — PROVED, NOT ASSUMED ***
column2: A DAUGHTER BORN LEIBHOLZ WHO MARRIED WOULD DIE UNDER HER HUSBAND'S NAME, so reading L could in principle miss her entirely. IT DOES NOT, BECAUSE THIS REGISTER FILES EVERY MARRIED WOMAN TWICE. Proved in Nr. 584: GERTRUD, died 2 January 1949, register Nr. 20, appears at page 217 as "Meyer geb. Hilfreich" under M AND at page 111 as "geb. Hilfreich verh. Meyer" under H — same woman, same date, SAME REGISTER NUMBER 20. The L block is therefore both places at once, and the negative covers married daughters as well as unmarried ones. RE-PROVE THIS IN EACH NEW VOLUME with one such pair; it costs three page reads and it is what makes the negative mean anything.

column1: # ---------------- THE METHOD, WHICH IS NOT NEGOTIABLE ----------------
*** RENDER ONCE OFFSCREEN, SHOW IN TWO OVERLAPPING HALVES ***
column2: the pane is about 600 px tall and a rendered page is 1100-1200. A full-page canvas RUNS OFF THE BOTTOM OF THE SCREENSHOT AND LOOKS COMPLETE. window.half(file, page, 'top'|'bot') renders at scale 2.0 to an offscreen canvas and draws half of it into a visible canvas, with a SIX PER CENT OVERLAP so no row falls down the seam. The overlap is verifiable: the top half's last number must appear in the bottom half.

column1: DO NOT TRUST window.innerHeight
column2: the emulated viewport and the captured image are two different things. innerHeight reported 1500 while screenshots came back 800x600. ONLY THE SCREENSHOT IS EVIDENCE.

column1: *** STAMP EVERY RENDER WITH ITS OWN PAGE NUMBER AND A CLOCK ***
column2: on page 214 the 'bot' call returned a screenshot PIXEL-IDENTICAL TO 'top' — the render had not repainted before the capture, and a whole half page would have been recorded as read without ever being seen. window.half now paints a black band across the top of the canvas reading PAGE n, TOP or BOT, the scale and a millisecond clock, and waits two animation frames plus 250 ms before returning. A DUPLICATE IS NOW VISIBLE IN THE IMAGE ITSELF rather than having to be noticed in the handwriting.

column1: *** AND FOR A SUSPECTED HIT: SCALE 6, SURNAME COLUMN ONLY ***
column2: window.crop(file, page, x0, x1, y0, y1, 6) with x roughly 0.06-0.45. AND READ THE NEIGHBOURING SURNAMES AT THE SAME MAGNIFICATION AS A CONTROL — if they are equally clear the hand is legible and the reading is not being forced onto a blur. That is how Günther Leibholz was confirmed.

column1: the search pattern is never the surname
column2: look for Le[iy][bp]h AND Laib- AND Leim- AND Leib-. The run has produced LEIMHOS, LEIBRANDT, LEIBRECHT, LEIB, LAIBENTHAL, LEIPEL, LEIPELT, LEIPOLD, LIEPOLD, LIEPOLT, LEYPOLDT and LEIPOLDT — every one a near miss, and LEIPHOLZ is a real spelling of this family's name.

column1: # ---------------- TWO TRAPS SPECIFIC TO WHAT IS LEFT ----------------
*** MULTI-YEAR VOLUMES HOLD MORE THAN ONE ALPHABET ***
column2: 1949-51, 1952-53, 1954-55, 1956-57, 1958-59, 1960-61 and 1962-63 are EACH SEVERAL YEARS IN ONE BOOK, and Kreuzberg 1982 proved that such a volume runs the alphabet through MORE THAN ONCE. Reading one L block and calling the volume done would miss two thirds of it. FIND EVERY L BLOCK: sample pages across the whole volume for L surnames before deciding where to read.
